\section{What the analysis notices}

  \item \finding{warning} \texttt{neighbor\_allgather/?} reports 0 messages but the fabric logged 12: the collective's own accounting disagrees with the traffic it produced.
  \item \finding{warning} \texttt{neighbor\_allgather/?} reports 0 messages but the fabric logged 12: the collective's own accounting disagrees with the traffic it produced.
  \item \finding{note} Collectives account for 72.5\% of the run's rank-seconds, so more of the pool's time went to coordination than to work.
  \item \finding{ok} All 11 checkable collective(s) sent exactly the number of messages their closed-form cost expression predicts.
  \item \finding{warning} 4 of 11 collective(s) disagree with the cost model on \emph{round} count while agreeing on messages: \texttt{barrier/dissemination} recorded 0 against 3, \texttt{barrier/central} recorded 0 against 2, \texttt{barrier/dissemination} recorded 0 against 3, \texttt{barrier/central} recorded 0 against 2. Rounds are the critical-path term, so a disagreement here changes predicted latency without changing predicted traffic.
\end{itemize}
